_provenance.note: Ohio citation authorities. Ohio uses TWO distinct authority families: Ohio Administrative Code rules (chapter:division-chapter-rule shape, e.g. '5101:4-2-02', '5101:4-4-23.3') and Ohio Revised Code statutory sections (chapter.section shape, e.g. '5101.84', '5101.548'). This pack prefixes OAC rules 'OAC <rule>' and ORC sections 'ORC <section>' to disambiguate and match the roster's convention of a short prefix per state's citation family (Wisconsin's FSH, Illinois' PM/WAG, Michigan's BEM/BAM, Pennsylvania's PAH).

patterns.note: Ohio Administrative Code Division 5101:4 (Food Stamps) rules, e.g. 5101:4-2-02, 5101:4-4-23, 5101:4-4-03
Ohio Revised Code sections, e.g. 5101.84 (drug-felony opt-out), 5101.548 (ABAWD waiver-request prohibition)

oacrule.note: categorically eligible assistance groups — OWF/SSI/PRC narrow pathway (no income test) AND the flat 200% FPL 'Ohio careline' broad-based pathway; waives 130% gross, net income, and resource limit for both
resource eligibility general policy — the $3,000/$4,500 standard, and its cross-reference to 5101:4-2-02 for the categorical-eligibility exemption
resource exclusions — vehicles excluded under Ohio's TANF-plan authority (Pub. L. 106-387 § 847); exact per-vehicle mechanics not spelled out in this rule's own text
deductions from income — standard deduction, excess medical (>$35, elderly/disabled only), child support (ordinary deduction, vendor payments count, alimony excluded), shelter/utility
certification periods — 36-month zero-earned-income elderly/disabled tier down to 4-6 month tier for ABAWD-member or unstable households
expedited service — 24-hour (72-hour w/ mitigating circumstances) zero-net-income tier, plus the federal-standard 7-day $150/$100 tier
able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) provisions — exemptions and work-requirement mechanics
elderly and disabled assistance group special rules, including Annual Reporter simplified-reporting status
definitions — includes the elderly/disabled definition used by the excess medical deduction and certification-period rules

orcsection.note: full statutory opt-out from the federal drug-felony SNAP ban — effective October 16, 2009, no conditions attached; independently confirmed by this pack, matches the already-verified snap-rules constant

prohibits ODJFS from requesting, applying for, or renewing an ABAWD geographic waiver — effective September 30, 2025 (enacted via HB 96); this pack found this CONTRADICTS the engine's current abawd_waiver_avail=true constant — see PROVENANCE.md
